questions.prompt: Order these locations by how APPROPRIATE it is for framework code to appear (most appropriate first).
questions.explanation: Framework code belongs at the edge (Main and adapters). It should not appear in use cases, and least of all in entities, where it would drag a volatile detail into the core.

questions.prompt: What is the 'asymmetric marriage' with a framework?

options.text: You and the framework share risk equally
You commit heavily to the framework, but it doesn't commit to you — its authors change and deprecate it on their schedule, so you carry the risk
The framework depends on your code

questions.explanation: You inherit, annotate, and structure around the framework; it evolves for its own reasons. Keeping it out of the core protects your most valuable code.

questions.prompt: The advice to keep a framework at arm's length so it can't dictate or invade your core is often phrased: don't ______ the framework.
questions.explanation: 'Don't marry the framework' — use it from the edge, behind your own abstractions, so it stays a replaceable plugin.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A detail/tool in the outer ring the core must not depend on
You commit to the framework, but it doesn't commit to you
Hiding a framework capability behind your own interface
How far a change (like an upgrade) can reach into your code

questions.explanation: Treat frameworks as details, wrap the capabilities the core needs behind your own interfaces, and keep them at the edge to shrink the blast radius of framework changes.

questions.prompt: Which practices keep a framework's blast radius small? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep entities and use cases framework-free
Use the framework in adapters and Main
Wrap framework capabilities behind your own interfaces
Annotate entities with ORM and serialization decorators

questions.explanation: Confining the framework to adapters/Main and wrapping it behind interfaces limits blast radius. Annotating entities drags the framework into the core.

questions.prompt: Does 'don't marry the framework' mean you should avoid frameworks?

options.text: No — use frameworks, but from the outer ring behind your own abstractions so they stay replaceable plugins
No — put frameworks in the entities layer

questions.explanation: Frameworks are useful; the point is to keep them at the edge as plugins rather than letting them become the platform your app is built inside.
